question.question: Can a leader demoted to learner with StepDownOnRemoval=false incorrectly authorize a ReadOnlySafe read via the singleton-voter shortcut, after the surviving voter has completed later writes?
question.importance: An invalid read barrier could let a caller following the documented application-index condition return a value older than writes completed before the read began. This concerns linearizable read safety, not read availability.
participants: Initial leader subsequently demoted to learner
Remaining sole voter elected as successor
objects: Register write completion and read result
contexts: StepDownOnRemoval=false for the discriminator; true as a protection control
AsyncStorageWrites=false; persistence and application completed before Advance
Single legal voter demotion leaving one voter plus one learner
event_paths: Elect initial leader -> propose and commit learner demotion -> apply it at both nodes -> isolate learner -> successor campaigns and applies writes -> read at learner -> bounded partial catch-up past returned read index -> consume register

supporting_behavior_ids.b-membership: Changes voter eligibility while optionally retaining the old leader role.

counterevidence: StepDownOnRemoval=true steps the demoted leader down.
Higher-term traffic and optional quorum checking can eventually step down the old leader, so schedule must preserve the read interval and still use legal message delays.
Safe reads normally use a quorum after current-term commit; only the singleton fast path bypasses this.
A ReadState alone does not establish stale client completion: caller must advance application past its index.
switchToConfig comment says demotions are prevented, but Changer.makeLearner and captured simple-demotion test support them.

Can bounded delivery advance the learner strictly past the returned index while leaving writes completed before read admission unapplied, producing an actual stale register read?
question.trigger_rationale: switchToConfig can retain StateLeader after demotion, IsSingleton checks voter cardinality without local membership, and the MsgReadIndex branch bypasses quorum exchange. Unlike the early-Advance and persistence-overlap leads, this history can use strict storage and application completion. A controlled API-driven demotion, successor writes and delayed learner catch-up can distinguish returned-but-unusable state from an actual stale read endpoint.

obligation.description: A ReadOnlySafe read begun after a register write has completed must not return an older register value when the caller consumes the matching ReadState after applying strictly beyond its returned index, assuming no later register write supersedes that completed write. This safety responsibility continues across a supported leader-to-learner demotion; returning no usable read result is not itself a violation.

scope.description: Linearizable ReadOnlySafe register reads using unique request contexts in a cluster with a legally committed/applied leader-to-learner demotion. The old leader remains a participating learner; no removed-node client service assumption is required.
assumptions: Serialized RawNode or Node operation; stable node identities.
Synchronous Ready handling persists Entries/HardState/Snapshot before messages and completes configuration/state-machine application before Advance.
Network may delay/drop messages; local storage does not fail; no Byzantine input.
Client writes complete only after committed application; a read starts later and consumes its matching ReadState only after applied index is strictly greater than returned index.
excluded: Early Advance, reused read contexts and uncommitted configuration injection
Unbounded read liveness; a missing result remains incomplete rather than a safety violation

grounding.derivation: ReadOnlySafe promises linearizable read requests. Node/RawNode ReadIndex promises that the matching read may be processed safely once application advances further than its returned index. For a deterministic register with no intervening later writes, that implies a read invoked after an acknowledged committed write must not return a prior register value when this application condition is met. Demotion is a supported membership operation and StepDownOnRemoval=false is accepted; its role-retention option does not state an exception to safe-read semantics. The check will use actual register application and strict applied>ReadState.Index, not presume index equality sufficient.
grounding.applicability: Caller completes storage and application before Advance, applies a committed simple voter demotion, and keeps the demoted learner in service under its public read API. No clock-dependent lease mode or synthetic reply is needed.
unresolved: The legal schedule and stale endpoint remain to be constructed and executed.
alternatives: Automatic stepdown or higher-term input can prevent the suspected result; include a protection control.
If the learner cannot pass the read barrier without catching up to the completed write, the proposed stale-read endpoint is excluded.

associations.rationale: Connect the public safe-read contract to the singleton optimization consuming local committed progress under a role whose membership may have changed.

bindings.description: ReadIndex singleton branch returns the local committed index without read quorum collection; subsequent branches otherwise defer or invoke safe quorum processing.
